scope: Owned capacity controller readiness and kernel resource controls only. No load, no capacity PASS, no p95, no N3.
external_review: P1-P8 proposal reviewed critically; not applied verbatim. Mount parsing alone is not treated as proof: each container is probed for kernel EROFS/ENOSPC/EFBIG behaviour.
design_decisions: Host xfs is mounted noquota, so no project/storage-opt quota exists. Durable controller output is a single launcher-created tar file bind-mounted alone; RLIMIT_FSIZE=256MiB caps it in the kernel (EFBIG). The previous writable artifact directory bind was removed.
controller.log written by the Docker CLI child is capped by RLIMIT_FSIZE=32MiB applied in preexec.

PostgreSQL/Redis run as their image users with cap-drop=ALL, read-only rootfs and log-driver none; their server logs go to their own kernel-sized tmpfs and are collected into the archive before removal.
Every writable tmpfs is read from each container's /proc/self/mountinfo, counted once per device; the 16MiB /dev/shm of each role is overfilled once to observe ENOSPC without inflating cgroup peaks.
Cleanup absence is proven by exact-name docker inspect returning not-found plus an empty run-label listing, never by an empty regex filter.
A global memory upper bound above 6GiB is NOT_PROVEN, not ERROR; swap peak or oom_kill makes the run INVALID.
Command timeouts keep partial output and are recorded per step; launcher timeout is recorded instead of escaping as a traceback.

runs.finding: Prototype could never run: Docker tmpfs /tmp defaults to noexec, so the git/docker wrappers raised PermissionError. Fixed with exec on the controller tmpfs; early failures now still write report.json.

PostgreSQL probe returned tmpfs=other: the probe wrote its own stderr into the tmpfs it had just filled. Controller tmpfs count also double-counted /dev file binds and the host /run socket. Fixed: stderr captured in a variable; tmpfs deduplicated by device; docker.sock explicitly allowed.

runs.limits: READY mode PG data tmpfs 1GiB; delivery mode allocates 2GiB and PG 1.5CPU/3GiB, app 2.25CPU/4.5GiB, still 4CPU/8GiB with Redis 0.2/384MiB and controller 0.05/128MiB.

runs.finding: check_capacity_environment.py --owned-controller run directly on the host fails before creating any resource (no cgroup cpu.max at host scope); labelled_remaining empty; sources unchanged.

gc_observer_negative.hypothesis: The test fetch ran gc.collect(2) synchronously inside the open-loop emitter. A full collection longer than the 50ms arrival gap delays the third worker past the 0.15s window, which correctly marks it arrival_window_closed. Full-collection time grows with heap size and swapped pages (host swap 100% used).
gc_observer_negative.evidence: Neighbour full collections in the preserved JUnit took 0.085-0.105s; the failed case 0.175s. Clean re-run: full collection 0.035s, 14/14 PASS twice. Deterministic reproduction: 4M-object ballast, full collection 0.341s -> FAIL. After fix (gc.collect(0) in fetch, still observable events) the same ballast (0.357s full collection) -> PASS; selection 14/14 PASS.
gc_observer_negative.classification: Test-design defect; observer and generator unchanged.
